children: Broader markets outperformed benchmark indices for the third consecutive week, with buying in banking, financial services, realty and capital market stocks helping Indian equities extend their winning streak despite concerns over rising inflation and interest rates.
The Nifty Smallcap 100 index rose 3.6 percent during the week ended November 13, while the Nifty Midcap 100 gained over 2 percent. Both indices recorded their third consecutive weekly advance.
The BSE Sensex gained 564.43 points, or 0.69 percent, to close at 81,592.45, while the Nifty 50 advanced 113.95 points, or 0.45 percent, to settle at 25,144.30.
The gains came despite Friday's decline, when the benchmarks snapped a three-session winning streak amid concerns over elevated crude oil prices and inflation.
Midcap and smallcap stocks lead gains

The rally in the Nifty Midcap 100 was led by Kalyan Jewellers India, PB Fintech, Hitachi Energy India, Bank of India, Motilal Oswal Financial Services and GE Vernova T&D India. These stocks gained between 10 percent and 18 percent during the week.
Page Industries, NHPC, Jubilant FoodWorks, Alkem Laboratories, Cochin Shipyard and Oracle Financial Services Software were among the laggards, declining 3–13 percent.
In the smallcap segment, Data Patterns (India), Aditya Birla Real Estate, Netweb Technologies India, Navin Fluorine International and Meesho were among the leading gainers.
Manappuram Finance, HBL Engineering, Zensar Technologies, Swan Corp, Narayana Hrudayalaya, Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals and Piramal Finance were among the stocks that ended the week lower.
PSU banks rally 7.5%, IT stocks lag
The Nifty PSU Bank index led sectoral gains, rising 7.5 percent during the week. The Nifty Media index climbed 5.2 percent, while the Nifty Capital Markets index advanced 3.8 percent.
Realty and pharma stocks also attracted buying interest, with both sectoral indices gaining around 2 percent.
The Nifty IT index was the biggest sectoral laggard, falling around 3.2 percent. Metal stocks also ended marginally lower.
FIIs buy Rs 33,343 crore; market wealth rises
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak for the third consecutive week, purchasing equities worth Rs 33,342.70 crore.
Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, remained net sellers for the second straight week, offloading shares worth Rs 24,191.81 crore.
The market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies increased by more than Rs 7 lakh crore during the week.
Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, said steady foreign inflows and better-than-expected second-quarter earnings helped markets absorb profit booking after the previous week's rally.
He said the earnings performance had also raised expectations of upgrades to FY27 estimates.
However, inflation emerged as a key concern.

A stronger-than-expected US consumer inflation reading reinforced expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike in December, while hawkish comments from Fed officials pushed global bond yields higher.
In India, October retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance limit of 6 percent as food prices increased.
Nair said investors continued to favour banks and financial stocks over IT, with foreign flows increasingly concentrated in large-cap financials.
He expects near-term consolidation, with investors likely to focus on earnings visibility, institutional flows and the outlook for monetary policy.
Stock market outlook: Key Nifty levels to watch next week
Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst, HDFC Securities
Shetti said the Nifty had witnessed a mild reversal after approaching resistance near 25,200, following its sharp advance in the previous week.
However, he maintained that the broader chart structure remained positive and that the current consolidation could present buying opportunities near support levels.
"The current weakness is expected to end soon by next week and the immediate supports to be watched at 24800-24700," he said.
He placed immediate resistance around 25,400, adding that a sustained move above this level could open the way for another round of gains.
Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking
Mishra said the Nifty's ability to hold the 24,800–25,000 zone would be crucial to maintaining the broader positive trend.
He advised investors to use market declines to accumulate quality stocks while avoiding contrarian positions.
His preferred sectors include banking, infrastructure, capital markets and realty, while he remains cautious on IT.
What will drive the market next week?

Investors will track US retail sales data, Nvidia's quarterly earnings and the minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting for clues on global interest rates and technology sector sentiment.
On the domestic front, attention will turn to the RBI's December policy review following the latest inflation reading.
Crude oil prices, foreign institutional flows and corporate earnings will remain key factors influencing market direction.
Nair expects markets to consolidate in the near term but sees support from large-cap valuations, earnings recovery prospects and a possible easing of geopolitical risks.
He recommended a selective approach, favouring companies with stronger earnings visibility.
